en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Surusuru Chapter.
56. The Training Rule on Food with Rice.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying among the Bhaggas at Susumāragira in the Bhesakaḷā Grove, in the Deer Park.
Now at that time, the monks were discarding bowl-washing water containing rice grains inside inhabited areas in the Kokanada Palace.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains inside inhabited areas, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?"
The monks heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so forth]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can these monks discard bowl-washing water containing rice grains inside a house?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, monks, that monks are throwing away bowl-washing water containing rice in inhabited areas?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can those foolish men discard bowl-washing water containing rice in a inhabited area?
This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:"
“The training should be observed: ‘I will not discard bowl-washing water containing rice-grains within an inhabited area.
Bowl-washing water containing rice-grains must not be discarded within an inhabited area.
Whoever, out of disrespect, discards bowl-washing water containing rice-grains within an inhabited area, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).”
There is no offense if it was unintentional,
or if there was a lack of mindfulness.
If, not knowing [the rule],
or being ill,
he takes it out, or breaks it, or places it in a receptacle, or carries it away and discards it;
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for the first offender.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
